newsitem.title: CHINA: Taiwan speech to European parliament angers China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan speech to European parliament angers China.

text.p: China slammed the European Parliament on Thursday for inviting the foreign minister of rival Taiwan to address the body, saying the move was gross interference in China's internal affairs.

"We express our firm opposition and strong indignation to this," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said when asked to comment on Taiwan Foreign Minister John Chang's scheduled address to the European Parliament in Brussels on Thursday.
"This seriously encroaches upon China's sovereignty and is also gross interference in China's internal affairs," he said.
Beijing and Taipei have been diplomatic rivals since the Communists won the Chinese civil war and drove Chiang Kai-shek and his defeated Nationalists into exile in Taiwan in 1949.
Chang, who bears his mother's surname, is a grandson of the late Nationalist leader.
China considers Taiwan a rebel province and has sought to push the island into diplomatic isolation in a quest to bring Taiwan under its rule.
Shen warned the European Parliament against harming bilateral relations.

"We sternly warn some people in the European Parliament...to stop any activity that undermines the reunification of China and harms friendly relations between China and European countries," the spokesman said.
Shen stressed there was only one China and that the People's Republic of China was the sole, legitimate government of all China with Taiwan as an inseparable part.
He said the European Parliament's adherence to the principle of "one China" was the foundation for developing relations.
Taiwan says it is committed to reunification with China, but only after the mainland embraces democracy and a free market economy.
China was less harsh to Australia, which recently played host to Taiwan's Minister without Portfolio Yang Shih-chien, according to media reports.
"The Australian government has stressed on many occasions that it will adhere to the 'one China' policy...We hope the Australian government will match its actions with its words," Shen said.
In Taipei, a tourism official blasted China for blocking Taiwan's attendance at an international tourism meeting in the Philippines.
Taipei's delegation boycotted the meeting's opening session on Thursday following Beijing's bitter complaints of the invitation from Manila.
